&api-questions;
The nbfx VCS API defines how a version control system tells the views that draw files the state of each: the VcsAnnotator contract and the VcsFileState enum. It is the first part of the M-tier version control contract and is devel until M2, when VcsProvider, VcsStatus and VcsHistoryProvider land: which annotator answers for a file when several are registered, how "no changes" is told from "not known yet", and the set of states are settled with them, and may change incompatibly until then.
A version control system registers a VcsAnnotator in the default lookup. A view asks every registered annotator for the state of the file of a row (stateOf) or of the changed files a folder holds (stateWithin) and takes the first answer; it listens for changes and asks again. The API is toolkit-free.
The Projects and Files trees colour the names of added, modified, deleted and conflicted files and badge the folders, packages and projects that hold them. Git answers from ide.vcs, out of the status it last read.
The contract is exercised through its Git implementation (GitStatusCacheTest in ide.vcs) and its consumer (VcsStatesTest in java.navigation). The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.

stateOf and stateWithin are called for every row a view draws, on the thread that draws it, and on any other: an annotator answers from what it already knows and must not read the disk or run a command. Change listeners are called on any thread.
No code runs on startup; the module holds an interface and an enum.
No code runs on exit.
